facts.text: - The releases repeat the 10-Q statement figures. For example the Q3 release states revenue "$ 1,107.3" and "$ 3,307.0" in millions (page:3), against 1,107,262 and 3,307,004 in thousands in the 10-Q (page:6). They agree after rounding. Treat the 10-Q as controlling and do not count the release as independent corroboration. - Maturity-table basis conflict (10-K). The debt table lists components that sum to 5,177,893 thousand before "Unamortized debt issuance costs (38,076)" and shows "Total debt $ 5,139,817" after them (page:100). The maturity table is captioned "excluding unamortized premiums and debt issuance costs" yet totals "Total debt maturities $ 5,139,817" (page:101), the net figure. The MD&A also says the aggregate principal "excludes $38.1 million in unamortized non-cash debt issuance costs" (page:46). The two captions cannot both describe the same total. The effect falls on any consumer that builds a maturity wall or compares principal to carrying value. This note only records the conflict; the arithmetic is shown under Calculations. - Liquidity text: the Q3 10-Q states "$1,513.7 million in borrowing capacity under the facility" and "we issued $1.3 million of letters of credit" (page:18). The 10-K states "$1,448.0 million" and "$47.0 million of letters of credit" at December 31, 2025 (page:102). Different dates, no conflict. The definition of the ratio is not in any supplied source. - Terminology: the registrant refers to "Bank Credit Facility" (the revolver) and "Term Loan" separately, and to the combined "bank credit agreement". Consumers should keep them as separate instruments.

facts.label: Analytical read-through
facts.text: - Usable coverage: the audited FY2025 statements, three 2026 interim 10-Qs and three releases support a reported-basis financial foundation for Q3 2026, nine months 2026, FY2025 and a last-twelve-months view built from FY2025 plus nine months 2026 less nine months 2025. All three components are located (10-K page:71; Q3 10-Q page:6). - Strongest contrary evidence: the bank credit agreement carries the only financial covenant described, a maximum leverage ratio, and the supplied text gives no definition of that ratio. A downstream module that computes its own leverage would not match the reported 3.69 without that definition, and the source set cannot settle the difference. Separately, the remainder of the debt after the 79% fixed share ("Approximately 79% of our total debt had a fixed interest rate", Q3 10-Q page:18) is floating-rate, so that pricing exposure rests on the term loan and revolver, whose terms are not supplied. - Source-risk mechanism: the maturity table and the debt table disagree on whether issuance costs are included. A reader who takes the maturity wall at face value could mix a net figure with gross principal. The 2027 bucket is the clearest case, because the 7.500% Senior Notes due April 2027 and the 4.625% Senior Notes due December 2027 both fall in it (10-K page:101, page:100). - Perimeter risk: consolidated balances include trust assets and matching trust liabilities ("Deferred receipts held in trust", "Care trusts’ corpus"). Total assets of this size are not corporate liquidity. - What cannot proceed: legal ranking, security, guarantor coverage and covenant testing on credit agreement definitions; any rating-based or market-price-based view, because no ratings, quotes or peers are supplied; anything after October 29, 2026. - Next evidence action: supply the Bank Credit Agreement and its November 2025 amendment, the senior indentures and supplements, any rating reports, and filings dated after October 29, 2026 up to the cutoff. Until then carry each limitation above into the modules.

- Source-risk mechanism: the maturity table and the debt table disagree on whether issuance costs are included. A reader who takes the maturity wall at face value could mix a net figure with gross principal. The 2027 bucket is the clearest case, because the 7.500% Senior Notes due April 2027 and the 4.625% Senior Notes due December 2027 both fall in it (10-K page:101, page:100).

- Perimeter risk: consolidated balances include trust assets and matching trust liabilities ("Deferred receipts held in trust", "Care trusts’ corpus"). Total assets of this size are not corporate liquidity.

- What cannot proceed: legal ranking, security, guarantor coverage and covenant testing on credit agreement definitions; any rating-based or market-price-based view, because no ratings, quotes or peers are supplied; anything after October 29, 2026.

- Next evidence action: supply the Bank Credit Agreement and its November 2025 amendment, the senior indentures and supplements, any rating reports, and filings dated after October 29, 2026 up to the cutoff. Until then carry each limitation above into the modules.

facts.label: Financial base view
facts.text: The reported financial base for SERVICE CORP INTERNATIONAL supports a stable consolidated credit view at September 30, 2026, with the leverage estimate and the covenant figure kept apart. Revenue for the nine months ended September 30, 2026 was 3,307,004 thousand against 3,197,707 thousand a year earlier, operating income rose to 728,292 thousand from 702,537 thousand, and operating cash flow was 869,288 thousand against 729,860 thousand. Total debt printed on the balance sheet was 5,172,948 thousand against 5,139,817 thousand at December 31, 2025, and cash fell to 172,653 thousand from 243,581 thousand, so net debt rose while the company bought back 318,942 thousand of stock and paid 145,421 thousand of dividends. No EBITDA appears in any source, so all EBITDA ratios below are analyst estimates built from printed operating income and printed depreciation and amortization lines (C1); they are not the covenant measure, which the credit agreement defines and the sources do not. The company reports a covenant leverage ratio of 3.69 against a 5.00 maximum at September 30, 2026. The stack is mostly unsecured senior notes plus a bank term loan and revolver due November 2030, with the revolver largely undrawn, and the one near-term maturity is the 7.500% notes due April 2027. Open items are the maturity-table basis conflict, a floating-rate average that does not match the debt note, and the absence of the credit agreement.

citations.quote: - **C1, EBITDA estimate.** Operating income + Depreciation and amortization + Amortization of intangibles (the latter two from the cash flow statement; the segment note shows them as separate lines, 10-K page:116). FY2024: 927,680 + 208,211 + 17,222 = 1,153,113. FY2025: 978,087 + 219,654 + 16,370 = 1,214,111. 9M 2025: 702,537 + 163,462 + 12,353 = 878,352. 9M 2026: 728,292 + 172,429 + 10,465 = 911,186. Amortization of cemetery property (FY2025 104,262; 9M 2026 74,592) is a cost of cemetery sales and is not added back. No divestiture gains, impairments or restructuring are adjusted, so this is a reported-basis estimate and not issuer-defined.

- **C5, debt basis.** Sum of printed components at December 31, 2025 before issuance costs: 136,924 + 550,000 + 750,000 + 850,000 + 800,000 + 800,000 + 750,000 + 255,000 + 54,766 + 151,061 + 80,142 = 5,177,893. Less 38,076 = 5,139,817, equal to the printed total debt and to the maturity-table total. At September 30, 2026: 136,924 + 550,000 + 750,000 + 850,000 + 800,000 + 800,000 + 735,938 + 235,000 + 110,852 + 160,547 + 76,092 = 5,205,353; less 32,405 = 5,172,948. Maturity table sum: 56,847 + 736,928 + 54,264 + 814,320 + 1,790,101 + 1,687,357 = 5,139,817. The caption says it excludes issuance costs, so either the caption or the amounts are mislabelled; which buckets carry the 38,076 reduction is Not determinable.

- **C6, net debt.** Carrying total debt less cash: FY2024 4,835,298 - 218,766 = 4,616,532; FY2025 5,139,817 - 243,581 = 4,896,236; March 31, 2026 5,162,816 - 257,959 = 4,904,857; June 30, 2026 5,303,165 - 260,411 = 5,042,754; September 30, 2026 5,172,948 - 172,653 = 5,000,295. All cash is treated as available, which overstates it, because part is encumbered.

- **C11, liquidity check.** Commitment less drawn less letters of credit equals the printed capacity: December 31, 2025 1,750.0 - 255.0 - 47.0 = 1,448.0; March 31, 2026 1,750.0 - 255.0 - 46.7 = 1,448.3; June 30, 2026 1,750.0 - 365.0 - 1.3 = 1,383.7; September 30, 2026 1,750.0 - 235.0 - 1.3 = 1,513.7. Liquidity at September 30, 2026 is 172.7 + 1,513.7 = 1,686.4 million US dollars (cash 172,653 thousand, part of it encumbered). Floating-rate instruments (term loan, revolver, headquarters facility) at September 30, 2026: 735,938 + 235,000 + 110,852 = 1,081,790, or 20.8% of gross principal 5,205,353, consistent with the printed "approximately 79%" fixed; which instruments are floating is an inference from the Level 3 classification and rates, and the sources do not list them.

rows.label: Reported results and liquidity are stable and covenant leverage is reported well inside its maximum. Our own leverage estimate is higher than the reported covenant figure because the covenant definition is not supplied.
Trailing leverage on our estimate is 4.15x gross and 4.01x net at September 30, 2026, against a reported covenant ratio of 3.69 and a maximum of 5.00.
Liquidity is cash plus undrawn revolver capacity of 1,513.7 million US dollars, with no revolver maturity before November 2030.
Operating cash flow after capital expenditure rose in the nine months of 2026, and shareholder returns used most of it.
Funeral gross profit fell in the nine months while cemetery gross profit rose, and the outlook for 2026 earnings was lowered after the quarter.
The annual maturity table does not match its own caption, and a stated floating-rate average conflicts with the debt note.

facts.label: Business and transaction view
facts.text: SERVICE CORP INTERNATIONAL is the largest listed deathcare operator in North America by its own account, running 1,491 funeral service locations and 506 cemeteries at September 30, 2026, of which 317 combine both. It has no sponsor, no controlling holder disclosed in the sources and no pending or completed transaction in the period under review, so the credit question is operating durability and capital allocation rather than deal structure. The business model sells at the time of need and in advance. Advance sales build a deferred revenue backlog, 17.72 billion US dollars at September 30, 2026, whose revenue is recognised mainly at death or delivery, so cash and revenue are separated in time and part of the backlog (insurance-funded, 9.15 billion US dollars) is not on the balance sheet. Pricing power and cemetery growth currently offset lower funeral volumes. Management keeps a leverage target of 3.5x to 4.0x and returns cash through dividends and buybacks within covenant limits that are not supplied. For creditors the key facts are the scale and diversification of the network, the visibility of the backlog, the concentration in three states, the trust and surety structure that sits behind preneed sales, and a consistent pattern of returning cash to shareholders through dividends and buybacks. The main open items are ownership and board detail (proxy statement not supplied), the credit agreement payment restrictions, and the ratings that are not in the sources.

facts.label: Transaction summary and new debt issues
facts.text: No acquisition of the issuer, sponsor investment, merger, spin-off or recapitalisation is described in the supplied sources, and the context lists no deal terms, quotes or ratings. The transaction row is therefore Insufficient Information, not an adverse conclusion. The financing events in the period under review are ordinary-course. In November 2025 the company amended its 2.2 billion US dollar credit agreement due January 2028 into a new 2.5 billion US dollar bank credit agreement due November 2030, made up of a 1.75 billion US dollar revolver (with a 100.0 million sublimit for letters of credit) and a 750.0 million US dollar term loan; at closing the term loan rose by a net 121.4 million and the revolver fell by a net 115.0 million (10-K page:102). The agreement is guaranteed by a majority of domestic subsidiaries and has a maximum leverage ratio and certain dividend and share repurchase restrictions. In September 2024 it issued 800.0 million US dollars of unsecured 5.750% Senior Notes due October 2032 (10-K page:102, page:123). A corporate headquarters debt facility due February 2037 funds the new headquarters; 110,852 thousand was drawn at September 30, 2026 (Q3 10-Q page:18), and its commitment size and terms are Not supplied. In the nine months to September 30, 2026 the company issued or added 586.1 million US dollars of debt, all on the revolver (530.0 million) and the headquarters facility (56.1 million), and paid 570.7 million, including 550.0 million on the revolver (Q3 10-Q page:19); no senior notes were issued or redeemed. On June 11, 2026 the board raised the repurchase authorization by about 472.0 million US dollars, and 498.8 million remained at September 30, 2026 (Q3 10-Q page:20). Subsequent to September 30, 2026 the company repurchased 232,968 shares for 18.2 million US dollars (Q3 10-Q page:20). The 7.500% Senior Notes due April 2027 are the nearest maturity and are within the current maturities of 195,060 thousand (CP-1). No new debt issue, refinancing or amendment dated after September 30, 2026 is in the sources.

facts.text: - Revenue durability. Evidence: backlog of 17.72 billion US dollars at September 30, 2026 and recognised preneed cemetery property revenue growth (Q3 10-Q page:31, page:40). Risk mechanic: revenue is recognised from earlier sales, which lowers volatility, but insurance-funded backlog is outside the balance sheet and future revenue exceeds trust assets (Q3 10-Q page:31). Credit implication: supports debt service visibility; the counter-evidence is falling funeral volume (nine-month services performed down 2.7%) and the lowered outlook, so the stability is revenue-side, not margin-side. No logged conflict counters this. - Margin and cash-flow risk. Evidence: Q3 and nine-month gross margin fell while selling compensation, advertising and health insurance costs rose (Q3 10-Q page:38, page:40; CP-1 calculation C12). Risk mechanic: a high fixed-cost base and front-loaded selling costs on preneed growth cut near-term margin. Credit implication: coverage ratios could ease if volume keeps falling; the covenant ratio reported at 3.69 is below its 5.00 maximum, but its definition is Not supplied, and the conflict on floating-rate cost (below) limits interest-cost conclusions. - Concentration risk. Evidence: California, Texas and Florida are three of the largest states by revenue and hold 32.2% of locations (10-K page:25, page:11; C2). Credit implication: creditors rely on management policy and covenant restrictions rather than a sponsor commitment; the restrictions are Not supplied, so legal capacity to increase distributions cannot be assessed. - Key uncertainties. rows.label: SERVICE CORP INTERNATIONAL is a widely held, listed, scale deathcare operator with a large deferred preneed backlog. No sponsor or transaction is disclosed, and its capital allocation favors shareholder returns within a stated leverage range.
The preneed backlog reached 17.72 billion US dollars at September 30, 2026, up from 17.01 billion at December 31, 2025.
Cemetery operations produce most segment gross profit, while funeral volumes are falling and funeral gross profit is lower in the nine months.
No transaction, sponsor or ownership change is disclosed; shareholder returns were partly debt-funded in FY2025 and covered by cash flow in the nine months of 2026.
Revenue and locations are concentrated in California, Texas and Florida, which management flags as exposed to natural disasters.

facts.label: Credit view
facts.text: SERVICE CORP INTERNATIONAL is a stable, cash-generative credit with moderate-to-high leverage that its liquidity comfortably supports. Its strongest support is a USD 17.72 billion preneed backlog, USD 1,686.4 million of liquidity at September 30, 2026 and a revolver and term loan that do not mature until November 2030. The weakest point is margin pressure: funeral volumes are falling, selling and healthcare costs are rising and the issuer lowered its 2026 earnings outlook, while distributions to shareholders stay high. Our estimated gross leverage of 4.15x is above the reported covenant ratio of 3.69x, and the covenant definition is not supplied. What decides the outcome is whether cemetery growth and pricing keep offsetting funeral volume loss without more debt-funded buybacks.

citations.quote: SERVICE CORP INTERNATIONAL is a stable, cash-generative credit with moderate-to-high leverage that its liquidity comfortably supports. Its strongest support is a USD 17.72 billion preneed backlog, USD 1,686.4 million of liquidity at September 30, 2026 and a revolver and term loan that do not mature until November 2030. The weakest point is margin pressure: funeral volumes are falling, selling and healthcare costs are rising and the issuer lowered its 2026 earnings outlook, while distributions to shareholders stay high. Our estimated gross leverage of 4.15x is above the reported covenant ratio of 3.69x, and the covenant definition is not supplied. What decides the outcome is whether cemetery growth and pricing keep offsetting funeral volume loss without more debt-funded buybacks.

facts.label: Key findings
facts.text: 1. Liquidity and maturities are the issuer's clearest strength. Cash of USD 172.7 million plus undrawn revolver capacity of USD 1,513.7 million gives USD 1,686.4 million, against current maturities of USD 195.1 million at September 30, 2026. The nearest bond maturity is USD 136.9 million of 7.500% notes due April 2027, then USD 550.0 million of 4.625% notes due December 2027. The revolver (USD 1,750.0 million commitment) and the term loan mature in November 2030 [CP-1 liquidity table and debt register]. 2. The debt stack is simple and mostly fixed-rate: six series of senior notes totalling USD 3,886.9 million, a USD 735.9 million term loan, a USD 235.0 million revolver draw, a USD 110.9 million headquarters facility, USD 160.5 million of finance leases and USD 76.1 million of mortgage and other debt. Total debt is USD 5,172.9 million at carrying value and USD 5,205.4 million before issuance costs. About 79% is fixed-rate. Security and guarantor terms for the notes are not supplied, so ranking cannot be assessed [CP-1 debt register; CP-0 gaps]. 3. Leverage is moderate-to-high on our estimate: 4.15x gross and 4.01x net on trailing EBITDA of USD 1,246.9 million built from printed operating income and depreciation and amortization, and interest cover of 4.87x on cash interest. The company reports a covenant leverage ratio of 3.69 against a maximum of 5.00 and targets 3.5x to 4.0x. No EBITDA appears in any source, so the covenant ratio cannot be rebuilt [CP-1 financials table]. 4. Operating results are mixed. Nine-month 2026 revenue rose 3.4% and operating income rose 3.7%, but the gross margin fell to 25.2% from 25.9%, funeral gross profit fell 5.5% on 2.7% fewer comparable services, and cemetery gross profit rose 5.3% [CP-1 calculation C12; CP-1A operating model]. On October 28, 2026 the issuer lowered its 2026 adjusted earnings per share outlook to USD 3.94 to 4.04 from USD 4.10 to 4.30 and kept its operating cash flow outlook midpoint at USD 1,085 million [CP-1A timeline]. 5. Cash generation is solid but is returned to shareholders. Operating cash flow less capital expenditure was USD 681.4 million for the last twelve months to Q3 2026 and USD 594.2 million in the nine months. Dividends and buybacks were USD 464.4 million in the nine months; in FY2025 they were USD 644.6 million, USD 90.3 million above operating cash flow less capital expenditure, while total debt rose USD 304.5 million [CP-1 calculations C3, CP-1A calculation C3]. 6. The debt stack is simple and mostly fixed-rate: six series of senior notes totalling USD 3,886.9 million, a USD 735.9 million term loan, a USD 235.0 million revolver draw, a USD 110.9 million headquarters facility, USD 160.5 million of finance leases and USD 76.1 million of mortgage and other debt. Nine-month 2026 revenue rose 3.4% and operating income rose 3.7%, but the gross margin fell to 25.2% from 25.9%, funeral gross profit fell 5.5% on 2.7% fewer comparable services, and cemetery gross profit rose 5.3% [CP-1 calculation C12; CP-1A operating model]. Operating cash flow less capital expenditure was USD 681.4 million for the last twelve months to Q3 2026 and USD 594.2 million in the nine months. ## Findings
### Reader summary
| Bottom line | Confidence | Main limitation |

| The seven supplied filings and releases are enough to start all four downstream modules on the consolidated company, with stated limits. Filed statements control; releases are supporting claims. | Medium | Credit agreement, indentures, ratings and a covenant EBITDA definition are not supplied, so legal terms and covenant headroom cannot be verified. |

### Readiness view

The effective source set can support the minimum module set for SERVICE CORP INTERNATIONAL with limitations. All seven issuer sources are filed SEC documents or furnished earnings releases of the single registrant, with text extracted from the original HTML. The audited FY2025 statements, three unaudited 2026 interim filings and three releases give a continuous record from December 31, 2025 to September 30, 2026. Nothing is blocked on identity. Each consumer is READY_WITH_LIMITATIONS. None is CONDITIONAL or BLOCKED. This is source sufficiency only; it does not say that downstream analysis is complete or that any model input contract is met.
### Information-availability boundary

- Every supplied document is dated on or before October 29, 2026, before the cutoff of 2026-11-05. The latest are the Q3 2026 release (Exhibit 99.1, "HOUSTON, Texas, October 28, 2026", `EX-99.1_2026-10-28…` page:2) and the Q3 2026 Form 10-Q, whose cover gives "The number of shares outstanding of the registrant’s common stock as of October 29, 2026 was 135,907,343" (`10-Q_2026-09-30…` page:1).
- Nothing dated between October 29, 2026 and the cutoff is supplied. Events in that window, for example new debt, acquisitions or rating actions, are Not supplied, not absent.

- The only post-balance-sheet event in the Q3 10-Q is a share repurchase: "Subsequent to September 30, 2026, we repurchased 232,968 shares for $18.2 million at an average cost per share of $78.21" (`10-Q_2026-09-30…` page:20). The 10-K likewise reports repurchases after December 31, 2025 (page:18, page:109).
- The Q3 10-Q text has no printed signature date in the extracted chunks (page:54 shows the signatory only). The date is taken from the cover and the release, not from a signature line.
### Identity and perimeter

- Reporting entity: Service Corporation International, a Texas corporation, "Commission file number 1-6402-1", listed on the New York Stock Exchange as SCI (`10-K_2025-12-31…` page:1; `10-Q_2026-09-30…` page:1). All statements are consolidated. The 10-Q defines the group as "companies owned directly or indirectly by Service Corporation International" (`10-Q_2026-09-30…` page:6).

- Units and currency: statements are in thousands of USD ("(In thousands, except per share amounts)", `10-Q_2026-09-30…` page:6). MD&A and the releases mix millions and thousands. No other currency is reported as a reporting currency. Canadian operations exist ("Due to cash balances residing in Canada", page:26), and a foreign currency translation line appears in comprehensive income (page:7). This matches the context currency USD.

- Debt perimeter: the bank credit agreement "is guaranteed by a majority of our domestic subsidiaries" (`10-Q_2026-09-30…` page:18; `10-K_2025-12-31…` page:102). Which subsidiaries guarantee, whether the senior notes carry guarantees, and the restricted or unrestricted split are not stated in the supplied text. The context leaves the guarantor list blank. This is an unresolved perimeter gap.

- Trust perimeter: merchandise, service and perpetual care trusts are consolidated and shown as "Deferred receipts held in trust" and "Care trusts’ corpus" (`10-Q_2026-09-30…` page:7); the notes say interests in the trusts "represent a liability to us" (page:12). Any consumer that reads total assets, liabilities or equity must separate trust balances from corporate balances.

- Auditor: PricewaterhouseCoopers LLP, Houston, "February 12, 2026", opinion on the financial statements and internal control, "We have served as the Company’s auditor since 1993" (`10-K_2025-12-31…` pages:68, 70). Interim statements are unaudited.
### Source register
#### Form 10-K for FY2025
- Family and authority: filed annual report, original authority for audited consolidated FY2025, FY2024 and FY2023 statements. Signed "Dated: February 12, 2026" (page:126).

- Located: statement of operations page:71, balance sheet page:72, cash flows pages:72 to 73, equity statement page:74, debt note pages:100 to 104 (debt components page:100, maturities page:101, bank credit agreement and activity pages:102 to 103, fair value pages:103 to 104), leases pages:105 to 107, commitments and contingencies pages:108 to 109, segments pages:115 to 116, liquidity and covenant table page:42, cash requirements pages:45 to 46, surety bonds page:46, business pages:7 to 18, risk factors pages:23 to 36.
- Period and basis: calendar years ended December 31, 2025, 2024 and 2023. Page:71 heads columns "2025 2024 2023".
- Limits: exhibits, including the credit agreement and indentures, are listed by reference only (pages:123 to 125); no exhibit text is supplied.
#### Forms 10-Q for Q1, Q2 and Q3 2026

- Family and authority: filed quarterly reports with unaudited condensed consolidated statements. Q1 signed "April 30, 2026", Q2 signed "July 30, 2026" (last chunks). Q3 shows no signature date in the text (see boundary above).

- Located in the Q3 10-Q: statement of operations page:6 (three and nine months ended September 30, 2026 and 2025), comprehensive income page:7, balance sheet page:7 (September 30, 2026 and December 31, 2025), cash flows pages:7 to 8 (nine months), equity pages:9 to 10, debt note pages:17 to 19, fair value pages:19 to 20, equity and repurchases page:20, segments pages:20 to 21, commitments and contingencies pages:22 to 23, liquidity and covenant table pages:25 to 26, financing activities and surety bonds pages:28 to 29, market risk page:51, Part II page:52.
- Located in the Q1 and Q2 10-Qs: statement of operations page:6, balance sheet page:7, cash flows page:7, debt note page:17, covenant table page:24, segments page:19.

- Period and basis: Q1 is three months; Q2 and Q3 carry both three-month and year-to-date columns. The cash flow statements are year-to-date, so a discrete quarter needs subtraction downstream. This module does not do it.
#### Earnings releases (Exhibit 99.1) for Q1, Q2 and Q3 2026

- Family and authority: issuer press releases furnished as Exhibit 99.1, unaudited and management-prepared. They give reported and "excluding special items" figures, guidance and comparable-location tables. Attributed claims only; the 10-Q controls where the two overlap.

- Located in the Q3 release: highlights and CEO comment page:2, key results table page:3, quarter narrative and outlook pages:4 to 6, balance sheet page:10, cash flows pages:10 to 11, comparable funeral results pages:12 to 15, comparable cemetery results page:16, non-GAAP reconciliation page:17, trust performance page:18. Q1 and Q2 releases have the matching tables (Q1: balance sheet page:8, operations page:9; Q2: balance sheet page:9, operations page:10).

- Non-GAAP: "Earnings excluding special items", "diluted earnings per share excluding special items" and "net cash provided by operating activities excluding special items" are the releases' own measures (page:4). No EBITDA, adjusted EBITDA or net debt measure appears in any supplied source; a search of all seven for "EBITDA" returned nothing.
### Document relationships and conflicts

- The releases repeat the 10-Q statement figures. For example the Q3 release states revenue "$ 1,107.3" and "$ 3,307.0" in millions (page:3), against 1,107,262 and 3,307,004 in thousands in the 10-Q (page:6). They agree after rounding. Treat the 10-Q as controlling and do not count the release as independent corroboration.

- Maturity-table basis conflict (10-K). The debt table lists components that sum to 5,177,893 thousand before "Unamortized debt issuance costs (38,076)" and shows "Total debt $ 5,139,817" after them (page:100). The maturity table is captioned "excluding unamortized premiums and debt issuance costs" yet totals "Total debt maturities $ 5,139,817" (page:101), the net figure. The MD&A also says the aggregate principal "excludes $38.1 million in unamortized non-cash debt issuance costs" (page:46). The two captions cannot both describe the same total. The effect falls on any consumer that builds a maturity wall or compares principal to carrying value. This note only records the conflict; the arithmetic is shown under Calculations.

- Liquidity text: the Q3 10-Q states "$1,513.7 million in borrowing capacity under the facility" and "we issued $1.3 million of letters of credit" (page:18). The 10-K states "$1,448.0 million" and "$47.0 million of letters of credit" at December 31, 2025 (page:102). Different dates, no conflict. The facility size ($1.75 billion revolving, $750.0 million term loan, "both due November 2030") is in the 10-K (page:102); the Q3 10-Q does not restate the revolver commitment.

- Covenant: the 10-K and each 10-Q give a "Per Credit Agreement 5.00 (Max)" level against an actual of 3.67 at December 31, 2025 (10-K page:42) and 3.69 at September 30, 2026 (Q3 10-Q page:25). The definition of the ratio is not in any supplied source.

- Terminology: the registrant refers to "Bank Credit Facility" (the revolver) and "Term Loan" separately, and to the combined "bank credit agreement". Consumers should keep them as separate instruments.

### Analytical read-through

- Usable coverage: the audited FY2025 statements, three 2026 interim 10-Qs and three releases support a reported-basis financial foundation for Q3 2026, nine months 2026, FY2025 and a last-twelve-months view built from FY2025 plus nine months 2026 less nine months 2025. All three components are located (10-K page:71; Q3 10-Q page:6).

- Strongest contrary evidence: the bank credit agreement carries the only financial covenant described, a maximum leverage ratio, and the supplied text gives no definition of that ratio. A downstream module that computes its own leverage would not match the reported 3.69 without that definition, and the source set cannot settle the difference. Separately, the remainder of the debt after the 79% fixed share ("Approximately 79% of our total debt had a fixed interest rate", Q3 10-Q page:18) is floating-rate, so that pricing exposure rests on the term loan and revolver, whose terms are not supplied.

- Source-risk mechanism: the maturity table and the debt table disagree on whether issuance costs are included. A reader who takes the maturity wall at face value could mix a net figure with gross principal. The 2027 bucket is the clearest case, because the 7.500% Senior Notes due April 2027 and the 4.625% Senior Notes due December 2027 both fall in it (10-K page:101, page:100).

- Perimeter risk: consolidated balances include trust assets and matching trust liabilities ("Deferred receipts held in trust", "Care trusts’ corpus"). Total assets of this size are not corporate liquidity.

- What cannot proceed: legal ranking, security, guarantor coverage and covenant testing on credit agreement definitions; any rating-based or market-price-based view, because no ratings, quotes or peers are supplied; anything after October 29, 2026.

- Next evidence action: supply the Bank Credit Agreement and its November 2025 amendment, the senior indentures and supplements, any rating reports, and filings dated after October 29, 2026 up to the cutoff. Until then carry each limitation above into the modules.

- Reading: the maturity-table total matches the net amount, not the 5,177,893 gross amount, despite its caption. Whether the individual annual buckets are net or gross is Not determinable from the text.

### Financial base view

The reported financial base for SERVICE CORP INTERNATIONAL supports a stable consolidated credit view at September 30, 2026, with the leverage estimate and the covenant figure kept apart. Revenue for the nine months ended September 30, 2026 was 3,307,004 thousand against 3,197,707 thousand a year earlier, operating income rose to 728,292 thousand from 702,537 thousand, and operating cash flow was 869,288 thousand against 729,860 thousand. Total debt printed on the balance sheet was 5,172,948 thousand against 5,139,817 thousand at December 31, 2025, and cash fell to 172,653 thousand from 243,581 thousand, so net debt rose while the company bought back 318,942 thousand of stock and paid 145,421 thousand of dividends. No EBITDA appears in any source, so all EBITDA ratios below are analyst estimates built from printed operating income and printed depreciation and amortization lines (C1); they are not the covenant measure, which the credit agreement defines and the sources do not. The company reports a covenant leverage ratio of 3.69 against a 5.00 maximum at September 30, 2026. The stack is mostly unsecured senior notes plus a bank term loan and revolver due November 2030, with the revolver largely undrawn, and the one near-term maturity is the 7.500% notes due April 2027. Open items are the maturity-table basis conflict, a floating-rate average that does not match the debt note, and the absence of the credit agreement.

A search of all seven sources for factoring, supply-chain finance, securitization and consent-decree language found no hits. Purchase commitments other than the items above are not disclosed in the sources read.
### Latest quarter and after

- Q3 2026 revenue was 1,107,262 thousand against 1,058,096 thousand; operating income was 252,890 thousand against 226,391 thousand, including a divestiture and impairment gain of 11,210 thousand against a loss of 415 thousand (Q3 10-Q page:6). Operating income excluding that line rose by 6.6%, and the gross margin fell to 24.6% from 25.1% (C12).

- Financing in Q3: the revolver balance fell from 365,000 to 235,000 thousand, the term loan from 740,625 to 735,938 thousand, and the headquarters facility rose from 106,620 to 110,852 thousand (debt register). Nine-month debt issuance was 586.1 million US dollars and payments 570.7 million (Q3 10-Q page:19). The Q3 10-Q debt note lists no senior note issuance or redemption in the nine months of 2026.

- Shareholder returns: the company repurchased 658,460 shares in Q3 (Q3 10-Q page:52) and 4,009,333 shares for 317.6 million US dollars in the nine months (page:20). The quarterly dividend was 0.36 US dollars per share in Q3 (page:26). The release says 464 million US dollars was returned year to date (Q3 release page:3).
- After the quarter: "Subsequent to September 30, 2026, we repurchased 232,968 shares for $18.2 million" (Q3 10-Q page:20). Shares outstanding were 135,907,343 at October 29, 2026 (page:1).

- Outlook (issuer claim): on October 28, 2026 the company set fourth quarter adjusted earnings per share at 1.10 to 1.20 US dollars and full-year adjusted earnings per share at 3.94 to 4.04 US dollars, citing lower funeral volumes than anticipated and higher healthcare, selling and advertising costs (Q3 release page:4). The July 29, 2026 range was 4.10 to 4.30 US dollars (Q2 release page:4), so the full-year range was lowered. The operating cash flow outlook midpoint of 1,085 million US dollars and maintenance capital expenditure of 335 million were unchanged, implying adjusted free cash flow of about 750 million (Q3 release page:4 to page:5).

- Apart from the repurchases and the outlook, the sources report no acquisition, debt issuance, rating action, litigation outcome or disaster event dated after September 30, 2026. Nothing dated after October 29, 2026 is supplied, so events from October 30, 2026 to the cutoff are Not supplied.
### Reconciliation to the readiness handoff

- Agreed: no EBITDA in any source; the executed credit agreement, indentures, guarantor detail and ratings are not supplied; the maturity table (10-K page:101) totals 5,139,817 thousand, the net carrying amount, although captioned as excluding issuance costs. That conflict is carried into the maturity chart above.

- Corrected: the readiness handoff listed discrete Q2 and Q3 cash flows as not printed. The Q3 release prints discrete Q3 net cash provided by operating activities (296.8 and 252.3 million US dollars) and total capital expenditures (99.5 and 101.6 million) on page:3 and page:17. These agree with C2. Other discrete Q3 cash flow lines are not printed and are derived.

- New conflict: the Q3 10-Q says the floating-rate debt "carried a weighted average rate of 4.1%, which is over 230 basis points lower than the weighted average rate for our floating rate debt in the prior year" (page:46). The debt note shows a floating-rate weighted average of 5.68% at September 30, 2026 and 5.54% at December 31, 2025 (page:18), and the bank credit agreement rate of 5.65% (page:18). The two cannot both describe the same population on a period-end basis. The sources do not explain it and no derivative or hedge is disclosed. This answer uses the debt-note rates and treats the 4.1% as unresolved.
- Note: the December 31, 2025 liquidity reading in the readiness handoff matches the 10-K (1,448.0 million).
## Calculations
All inputs are printed figures cited above, in USD thousands unless stated. Results are rounded as shown.

- **C1, EBITDA estimate.** Operating income + Depreciation and amortization + Amortization of intangibles (the latter two from the cash flow statement; the segment note shows them as separate lines, 10-K page:116). FY2024: 927,680 + 208,211 + 17,222 = 1,153,113. FY2025: 978,087 + 219,654 + 16,370 = 1,214,111. 9M 2025: 702,537 + 163,462 + 12,353 = 878,352. 9M 2026: 728,292 + 172,429 + 10,465 = 911,186. Amortization of cemetery property (FY2025 104,262; 9M 2026 74,592) is a cost of cemetery sales and is not added back. No divestiture gains, impairments or restructuring are adjusted, so this is a reported-basis estimate and not issuer-defined.

- **C5, debt basis.** Sum of printed components at December 31, 2025 before issuance costs: 136,924 + 550,000 + 750,000 + 850,000 + 800,000 + 800,000 + 750,000 + 255,000 + 54,766 + 151,061 + 80,142 = 5,177,893. Less 38,076 = 5,139,817, equal to the printed total debt and to the maturity-table total. At September 30, 2026: 136,924 + 550,000 + 750,000 + 850,000 + 800,000 + 800,000 + 735,938 + 235,000 + 110,852 + 160,547 + 76,092 = 5,205,353; less 32,405 = 5,172,948. Maturity table sum: 56,847 + 736,928 + 54,264 + 814,320 + 1,790,101 + 1,687,357 = 5,139,817. The caption says it excludes issuance costs, so either the caption or the amounts are mislabelled; which buckets carry the 38,076 reduction is Not determinable.

- **C6, net debt.** Carrying total debt less cash: FY2024 4,835,298 - 218,766 = 4,616,532; FY2025 5,139,817 - 243,581 = 4,896,236; March 31, 2026 5,162,816 - 257,959 = 4,904,857; June 30, 2026 5,303,165 - 260,411 = 5,042,754; September 30, 2026 5,172,948 - 172,653 = 5,000,295. All cash is treated as available, which overstates it, because part is encumbered.

- **C11, liquidity check.** Commitment less drawn less letters of credit equals the printed capacity: December 31, 2025 1,750.0 - 255.0 - 47.0 = 1,448.0; March 31, 2026 1,750.0 - 255.0 - 46.7 = 1,448.3; June 30, 2026 1,750.0 - 365.0 - 1.3 = 1,383.7; September 30, 2026 1,750.0 - 235.0 - 1.3 = 1,513.7. Liquidity at September 30, 2026 is 172.7 + 1,513.7 = 1,686.4 million US dollars (cash 172,653 thousand, part of it encumbered). Floating-rate instruments (term loan, revolver, headquarters facility) at September 30, 2026: 735,938 + 235,000 + 110,852 = 1,081,790, or 20.8% of gross principal 5,205,353, consistent with the printed "approximately 79%" fixed; which instruments are floating is an inference from the Level 3 classification and rates, and the sources do not list them.

- Question: which transaction, business, ownership and operating facts matter most to a creditor, and what is the issuer's documented capital allocation and governance behaviour? Decision drivers: transaction and ownership structure; business and operating model; credit-relevant history or change.

## Findings
### Reader summary
| Bottom line | Confidence | Main limitation |

| SERVICE CORP INTERNATIONAL is a widely held, listed, scale deathcare operator with a large deferred preneed backlog. No sponsor or transaction is disclosed, and its capital allocation favors shareholder returns within a stated leverage range. | Medium | Ownership percentages, the credit agreement's payment restrictions and any ratings are not supplied, so control and creditor protections cannot be assessed. |
| Finding | Creditor impact | Confidence |

| The preneed backlog reached 17.72 billion US dollars at September 30, 2026, up from 17.01 billion at December 31, 2025. | Deferred revenue gives revenue visibility, but part is insurance-funded and sits outside the balance sheet. | High |

| Cemetery operations produce most segment gross profit, while funeral volumes are falling and funeral gross profit is lower in the nine months. | Earnings rely on pricing and cemetery growth to offset volume loss. | Medium |

| No transaction, sponsor or ownership change is disclosed; shareholder returns were partly debt-funded in FY2025 and covered by cash flow in the nine months of 2026. | Event risk looks low, but payment restrictions and baskets cannot be checked. | Medium |

| Revenue and locations are concentrated in California, Texas and Florida, which management flags as exposed to natural disasters. | A regional event could affect cash flow across a large share of the network. | Medium |
### Business and transaction view

SERVICE CORP INTERNATIONAL is the largest listed deathcare operator in North America by its own account, running 1,491 funeral service locations and 506 cemeteries at September 30, 2026, of which 317 combine both. It has no sponsor, no controlling holder disclosed in the sources and no pending or completed transaction in the period under review, so the credit question is operating durability and capital allocation rather than deal structure. The business model sells at the time of need and in advance. Advance sales build a deferred revenue backlog, 17.72 billion US dollars at September 30, 2026, whose revenue is recognised mainly at death or delivery, so cash and revenue are separated in time and part of the backlog (insurance-funded, 9.15 billion US dollars) is not on the balance sheet. Pricing power and cemetery growth currently offset lower funeral volumes. Management keeps a leverage target of 3.5x to 4.0x and returns cash through dividends and buybacks within covenant limits that are not supplied. For creditors the key facts are the scale and diversification of the network, the visibility of the backlog, the concentration in three states, the trust and surety structure that sits behind preneed sales, and a consistent pattern of returning cash to shareholders through dividends and buybacks. The main open items are ownership and board detail (proxy statement not supplied), the credit agreement payment restrictions, and the ratings that are not in the sources.

### Transaction summary and new debt issues

The transaction row is therefore Insufficient Information, not an adverse conclusion. The financing events in the period under review are ordinary-course. In November 2025 the company amended its 2.2 billion US dollar credit agreement due January 2028 into a new 2.5 billion US dollar bank credit agreement due November 2030, made up of a 1.75 billion US dollar revolver (with a 100.0 million sublimit for letters of credit) and a 750.0 million US dollar term loan; at closing the term loan rose by a net 121.4 million and the revolver fell by a net 115.0 million (10-K page:102). In the nine months to September 30, 2026 the company issued or added 586.1 million US dollars of debt, all on the revolver (530.0 million) and the headquarters facility (56.1 million), and paid 570.7 million, including 550.0 million on the revolver (Q3 10-Q page:19); no senior notes were issued or redeemed. On June 11, 2026 the board raised the repurchase authorization by about 472.0 million US dollars, and 498.8 million remained at September 30, 2026 (Q3 10-Q page:20). Subsequent to September 30, 2026 the company repurchased 232,968 shares for 18.2 million US dollars (Q3 10-Q page:20). The 7.500% Senior Notes due April 2027 are the nearest maturity and are within the current maturities of 195,060 thousand (CP-1). | After September 30, 2026 | Repurchased 232,968 shares for 18.2 million US dollars (subsequent event) | Documentary Fact | Q3 10-Q page:20 |
### Credit translations

- **Revenue durability.** Evidence: backlog of 17.72 billion US dollars at September 30, 2026 and recognised preneed cemetery property revenue growth (Q3 10-Q page:31, page:40). Risk mechanic: revenue is recognised from earlier sales, which lowers volatility, but insurance-funded backlog is outside the balance sheet and future revenue exceeds trust assets (Q3 10-Q page:31). Credit implication: supports debt service visibility; the counter-evidence is falling funeral volume (nine-month services performed down 2.7%) and the lowered outlook, so the stability is revenue-side, not margin-side. No logged conflict counters this.

- **Margin and cash-flow risk.** Evidence: Q3 and nine-month gross margin fell while selling compensation, advertising and health insurance costs rose (Q3 10-Q page:38, page:40; CP-1 calculation C12). Risk mechanic: a high fixed-cost base and front-loaded selling costs on preneed growth cut near-term margin. Credit implication: coverage ratios could ease if volume keeps falling; the covenant ratio reported at 3.69 is below its 5.00 maximum, but its definition is Not supplied, and the conflict on floating-rate cost (below) limits interest-cost conclusions.

- **Concentration risk.** Evidence: California, Texas and Florida are three of the largest states by revenue and hold 32.2% of locations (10-K page:25, page:11; C2). Risk mechanic: a single catastrophe or regulatory change in these states hits many locations at once. Credit implication: insurance and surety capacity matter; revenue by state is Not supplied.

- **Sponsor and capital allocation alignment.** Evidence: dividend payout target, buyback pace and leverage target (10-K page:18; Q3 10-Q page:20, page:25). Risk mechanic: returns to shareholders are discretionary and sized to cash flow; in FY2025 they exceeded operating cash flow less capex. Credit implication: creditors rely on management policy and covenant restrictions rather than a sponsor commitment; the restrictions are Not supplied, so legal capacity to increase distributions cannot be assessed.
- **Key uncertainties.** Ratings, credit agreement terms, guarantor and security detail for the notes, ownership percentages and the proxy statement are not in the sources.
### Conflicts logged
The conflicts are logged as found and are not reconciled.
| Conflict | Span A | Span B | Downstream effect |

| Floating-rate cost | "our floating-rate debt carried a weighted average rate of 4.1%, which is over 230 basis points lower than the weighted average rate for our floating rate debt in the prior year" (Q3 10-Q page:46) | Floating debt weighted average interest rate "5.68 %" at September 30, 2026 and "5.54 %" at December 31, 2025 (Q3 10-Q page:18) | Interest-cost and rate-sensitivity statements for the revolver and term loan are unsettled; the debt-note rates are used meanwhile |

| Maturity table basis | Maturity table "excluding unamortized premiums and debt issuance costs" totals 5,139,817 thousand (10-K page:101) | "Total debt" after "Unamortized debt issuance costs (38,076)" is also 5,139,817 thousand (10-K page:100) | The annual maturity wall may be on a net basis; which buckets are net is Not determinable |
### Consumer readiness
| Consumer | Readiness | What it should take from this module | Why it matters | Gap and required action |

| CP-2 | READY_WITH_LIMITATIONS | Backlog and preneed funding model, concentration, distribution behaviour and leverage policy, the lowered outlook, nearest maturity | Liquidity and covenant work needs the behaviour of distributions against cash flow and the scale of off-balance-sheet insurance backlog | Credit agreement payment restrictions, indentures, ratings and ownership detail not supplied; obtain them |

| CP-5 | READY_WITH_LIMITATIONS | Each fact row with its category and locator, and the two logged conflicts | Review needs the Management Language rows kept apart from Documentary Facts | The market share, outlook and cash-flow neutral claims are issuer statements and need to stay attributed |
## Calculations

- **C1, mix.** Revenue mix, nine months 2026 (USD thousands): funeral revenue 1,838,004 and cemetery revenue 1,469,000 against total revenue 3,307,004: 1,838,004 / 3,307,004 = 55.6% and 1,469,000 / 3,307,004 = 44.4%. Segment gross profit: funeral 349,185 and cemetery 483,040 against 832,225: 349,185 / 832,225 = 42.0% and 483,040 / 832,225 = 58.0%. Geography: United States 3,148,755 / 3,307,004 = 95.2% and Canada 158,249 / 3,307,004 = 4.8% (Q3 10-Q page:21).

- **C2, concentration.** Locations at December 31, 2025 from the 10-K table: California 166 + 43 = 209; Florida 137 + 64 = 201; Texas 164 + 65 = 229. 209 + 201 + 229 = 639. 639 / 1,985 = 32.2% (10-K page:11). This is a location count, not a revenue share.

- **C3, distributions against free cash flow (CP-1 table values).** FY2025 dividends 183,571 + buybacks 461,015 = 644,586; operating cash flow less capex 554,245 (CP-1 C3); difference 644,586 - 554,245 = 90,341 funded from other sources. Total debt 5,139,817 - 4,835,298 = 304,519 higher at December 31, 2025 than a year earlier (carrying value). Nine months 2026: dividends 145,421 + buybacks 318,942 = 464,363 against operating cash flow less capex 594,241; 594,241 - 464,363 = 129,878 (CP-1 C3).

| Credit agreement payment restrictions and baskets, covenant definition, indentures | High | CP-2 | Supply executed documents |

| Headquarters debt facility commitment and terms | Low | CP-2 | Supply facility terms |
| Floating-rate and maturity-table conflicts (logged above) | Medium | CP-2 | Confirm in filed HTML or with the issuer |
| Events after October 29, 2026 to the cutoff | Medium | CP-2 | Supply later 8-Ks or confirm none |
## Next module

- CP-2: start from the CP-1 debt register and liquidity; use the behaviour assessment (Neutral or Mixed, with distributions partly debt-funded in FY2025) as context, not as a score; keep the 4.1% rate claim out of interest-sensitivity work until resolved; treat management's stated 3.5x to 4.0x leverage range as policy only.

## Request

SERVICE CORP INTERNATIONAL (issuer id `sci`), as of 2026-11-05, pathway credit_snapshot, current period Q3 2026 and prior period FY2025 in USD. This module synthesises the fundamental credit view from the CP-1 financial base and the CP-1A business context, using upstream handoffs only. It gives no peer ranking, instrument recommendation or recovery conclusion.
## Sources
CP-2 reads the two upstream handoffs and the readiness handoff; it quotes no source text. The issuer sources behind them are listed for traceability.
| Source | sha256 | Role |
| 10-K_2025-12-31_sci-20251231.htm.jsonl | 36f224c032003fbd2390907d9603b5b257c583b876df570b13d8b342fe4f5f00 | FY2025 annual report behind the upstream figures |

| EX-99.1_2026-10-28_exhibit991q326earningsrele.htm.jsonl | d5fe76c2497f82e8e53c22501a405cf8fb7df74cae0b9bd5b7f0b933f384c2b3 | Q3 2026 earnings release, revised outlook |
| context | 65d65475c254be68b493ea4436b1695cdda5a813079114b87a550c9ce00dd797 | Run settings; not issuer evidence |
Supplied handoffs:
| Module | sha256 | Use |
| CP-0 | a4424fa5ae507987bbabfc0ea081c1e6d0634859958366cc6d6a3e21db770495 | Source readiness and inherited limits |
| CP-1 | b2929721b6dd1fe38c8e3fe6a91d3ab13c7f3197b5f3265b7ede5c6f6e3cdc9f | Financial base, debt register, liquidity, covenant as reported, claims outside debt |
| CP-1A | b01abf4ad8bf7d83bda476fbd5b626e74996926a7ff4ea4e5b5602e926d1af16 | Business model, ownership, capital allocation behaviour, conflicts, readiness of this module |
## Findings
### Reader summary
| Bottom line | Confidence | Main limitation |

| The company looks like a stable, cash-generative credit with moderate-to-high leverage, ample liquidity and distant maturities. Its estimated leverage is above the reported covenant figure, and shareholder returns are the main discretionary use of cash. | Medium | The covenant definition, credit agreement and ratings are not supplied, so headroom and creditor protections cannot be verified. |
| Finding | Creditor impact | Confidence |
| Liquidity is 1,686.4 million US dollars and the revolver and term loan mature in November 2030. | Maturities through April 2027 and December 2027 are well covered. | High |

| Estimated gross leverage is 4.15x and net leverage 4.01x, against a reported covenant ratio of 3.69 and a maximum of 5.00. | Reported headroom is wide, but our estimate cannot be tied to the covenant. | Medium |

| Funeral volumes and gross profit are falling, cemetery earnings are rising, and the 2026 earnings outlook was lowered after the quarter. | Margins are under pressure from selling and healthcare costs. | Medium |

| Shareholder returns exceeded operating cash flow after capital expenditure in FY2025 and were covered by it in the nine months of 2026. | Debt reduction is not the priority; leverage stays near its target range. | Medium |
### Credit view

SERVICE CORP INTERNATIONAL is a stable, cash-generative credit with moderate-to-high leverage that its liquidity comfortably supports. Its strongest support is a USD 17.72 billion preneed backlog, USD 1,686.4 million of liquidity at September 30, 2026 and a revolver and term loan that do not mature until November 2030. The weakest point is margin pressure: funeral volumes are falling, selling and healthcare costs are rising and the issuer lowered its 2026 earnings outlook, while distributions to shareholders stay high. Our estimated gross leverage of 4.15x is above the reported covenant ratio of 3.69x, and the covenant definition is not supplied. What decides the outcome is whether cemetery growth and pricing keep offsetting funeral volume loss without more debt-funded buybacks.
### Key findings

1. Liquidity and maturities are the issuer's clearest strength. Cash of USD 172.7 million plus undrawn revolver capacity of USD 1,513.7 million gives USD 1,686.4 million, against current maturities of USD 195.1 million at September 30, 2026. The nearest bond maturity is USD 136.9 million of 7.500% notes due April 2027, then USD 550.0 million of 4.625% notes due December 2027. The revolver (USD 1,750.0 million commitment) and the term loan mature in November 2030 [CP-1 liquidity table and debt register].

2. The debt stack is simple and mostly fixed-rate: six series of senior notes totalling USD 3,886.9 million, a USD 735.9 million term loan, a USD 235.0 million revolver draw, a USD 110.9 million headquarters facility, USD 160.5 million of finance leases and USD 76.1 million of mortgage and other debt. Total debt is USD 5,172.9 million at carrying value and USD 5,205.4 million before issuance costs. About 79% is fixed-rate. Security and guarantor terms for the notes are not supplied, so ranking cannot be assessed [CP-1 debt register; CP-0 gaps].

3. Leverage is moderate-to-high on our estimate: 4.15x gross and 4.01x net on trailing EBITDA of USD 1,246.9 million built from printed operating income and depreciation and amortization, and interest cover of 4.87x on cash interest. The company reports a covenant leverage ratio of 3.69 against a maximum of 5.00 and targets 3.5x to 4.0x. No EBITDA appears in any source, so the covenant ratio cannot be rebuilt [CP-1 financials table].

4. Operating results are mixed. Nine-month 2026 revenue rose 3.4% and operating income rose 3.7%, but the gross margin fell to 25.2% from 25.9%, funeral gross profit fell 5.5% on 2.7% fewer comparable services, and cemetery gross profit rose 5.3% [CP-1 calculation C12; CP-1A operating model]. On October 28, 2026 the issuer lowered its 2026 adjusted earnings per share outlook to USD 3.94 to 4.04 from USD 4.10 to 4.30 and kept its operating cash flow outlook midpoint at USD 1,085 million [CP-1A timeline].

5. Cash generation is solid but is returned to shareholders. Operating cash flow less capital expenditure was USD 681.4 million for the last twelve months to Q3 2026 and USD 594.2 million in the nine months. Dividends and buybacks were USD 464.4 million in the nine months; in FY2025 they were USD 644.6 million, USD 90.3 million above operating cash flow less capital expenditure, while total debt rose USD 304.5 million [CP-1 calculations C3, CP-1A calculation C3].

6. Visibility is supported by the backlog, which grew to USD 17.72 billion from USD 17.01 billion, but USD 9.15 billion is insurance-funded and not on the balance sheet, and future revenue exceeds trust assets, so cash received can lag revenue recognised [CP-1A operating model].

7. Claims outside debt are modest relative to debt except trust and surety structures: operating leases (present value USD 50.8 million at December 31, 2025), unfunded retirement plans (USD 12.3 million), surety bonds of USD 498.3 million and unquantified unclaimed property audits in about forty states. Consolidated trust balances of USD 6,050.7 million and USD 2,448.4 million are matched by trust assets [CP-1 claims table].

8. Two source conflicts are unresolved: the floating-rate average of 4.1% against 5.68% in the debt note, and the annual maturity table, whose caption and total do not agree. Interest sensitivity and the maturity ladder rest on the debt note and carrying values meanwhile [CP-1A conflicts].
### Strengths and weaknesses

Strengths. Scale and diversification: the network of 1,491 funeral service locations and 506 cemeteries, with a cemetery segment protected by high barriers to entry, spreads local demand risk [Documentary Fact; CP-1A operating model]. Revenue visibility: the preneed backlog of USD 17.72 billion is recognised over time [Documentary Fact]. Liquidity and maturity profile: USD 1,686.4 million of liquidity and a bank facility maturing in November 2030 [Documentary Fact; CP-1]. Cash conversion: operating cash flow after capital expenditure of USD 681.4 million for the last twelve months to Q3 2026, equal to 13.2% of total debt [Analyst Interpretation; CP-1 C3 and C10]. Fixed-rate mix: about 79% of debt is fixed at a weighted average of 4.67%, which limits near-term interest cost swings [Documentary Fact; CP-1].

Weaknesses. Margin pressure: higher selling compensation, advertising and healthcare costs against falling funeral volumes in a high fixed-cost business, with a lowered 2026 outlook [Documentary Fact and Management Language; CP-1A]. Leverage that is moderate-to-high on our estimate at 4.15x gross, with a covenant definition that is not supplied and a management target of 3.5x to 4.0x [Analyst Interpretation; CP-1]. Distributions: dividends and buybacks absorb most free cash flow, so debt reduction is unlikely without a policy change [Analyst Interpretation; CP-1A governance]. Concentration: 32.2% of locations are in California, Texas and Florida, which the issuer itself flags as exposed to natural disasters [Documentary Fact and Analyst Interpretation; CP-1A]. Preneed structure: surety bonds of USD 498.3 million and a USD 258.7 million trust-funding obligation if surety were not renewed at December 31, 2025 are contingent liquidity calls [Documentary Fact; CP-1A]. Missing creditor protections: the credit agreement restrictions, indentures, guarantor detail and ratings are not supplied [Insufficient Information].
### Credit assessment
| Assessment | Category | Confidence | Basis |

| Fundamental credit view: stable, cash-generative operator with moderate-to-high leverage, ample liquidity and no refinancing pressure before 2027; margin pressure and shareholder-return policy are the main watch items | Analyst Interpretation | Medium | CP-1 financials, liquidity and debt register; CP-1A operating model and governance rows |

| Business risk: low to moderate, supported by scale, backlog visibility and a defensive demand pattern, offset by funeral volume decline and state concentration | Analyst Interpretation | Medium | CP-1A company and operating model |
| Financial risk: moderate to high on our estimated 4.15x gross leverage; liquidity strong | Analyst Interpretation | Medium | CP-1 financials table |

| Creditor protection and ranking | Insufficient Information | Insufficient Information | Credit agreement, indentures, guarantor and security detail and ratings are not supplied; this limits legal capacity, ranking and covenant conclusions |
Confidence is below High because the upstream readiness judgments for this module are READY_WITH_LIMITATIONS and the upstream gaps ledger lists a High-severity covenant-definition gap.
### Thesis

SERVICE CORP INTERNATIONAL is a defensive, scale-driven deathcare operator whose backlog, cash flow and long-dated bank facility support its moderate-to-high leverage, provided cemetery growth and pricing keep offsetting funeral volume loss and shareholder returns do not outrun cash flow.
### Key credit risks
| Risk | Mechanic | Credit implication | Severity | Basis |

| Margin compression | Selling compensation, advertising and healthcare costs rise ahead of preneed revenue recognition; fixed costs amplify volume loss | Coverage and leverage ratios could weaken even with stable revenue; the lowered outlook shows it has begun | Material | CP-1 C12; CP-1A operating model |

| Covenant and definition uncertainty | The only financial covenant is a maximum leverage ratio on an unsupplied definition; our estimate is above the reported figure | Headroom cannot be verified; a definition that is stricter than reported could change the picture | Material | CP-1 financials; CP-0 gap |

| Distribution policy | Dividends and buybacks sized to cash flow, partly debt-funded in FY2025; restrictions not supplied | Leverage can drift at the upper end of the stated range without a contractual limit evident | Material | CP-1A governance; CP-1 C3 |

| Regional concentration | A third of locations in three disaster-prone states | One event can disrupt cash flow and test insurance; revenue by state not supplied | Material | CP-1A concentration row |

| Preneed trust and surety calls | Surety bonds and trust funding rules; unquantified unclaimed property audits | A loss of surety capacity would require cash funding of trusts | Minor | CP-1A regulatory row; CP-1 claims table |

| Refinancing of 2027 maturities | USD 136.9 million due April 2027 and USD 550.0 million due December 2027 against liquidity of USD 1,686.4 million | Low near-term risk; any refinancing of the 4.625% notes would be at then-current rates, which the sources do not give | Minor | CP-1 debt register |

| Floating-rate exposure | About 21% of debt floats on the term loan, revolver and headquarters facility; a rate average in the 10-Q conflicts with the debt note | Interest cost sensitivity is unsettled; modest relative to cash flow | Minor | CP-1A conflicts |
### Debt, liquidity and covenant summary
| Item | Figure | Category | Basis |
| Total debt, carrying value, September 30, 2026 | USD 5,172.9 million (USD 5,205.4 million before issuance costs) | Documentary Fact | CP-1 debt register |
| Cash | USD 172.7 million, part of it encumbered | Documentary Fact | CP-1 liquidity table |
| Undrawn bank credit facility capacity | USD 1,513.7 million (commitment USD 1,750.0 million, drawn USD 235.0 million, letters of credit USD 1.3 million) | Documentary Fact | CP-1 liquidity table |
| Liquidity | USD 1,686.4 million | Analyst Interpretation | CP-1 C11 |
| Current maturities | USD 195.1 million | Documentary Fact | CP-1 maturities chart row |
| Fixed-rate share and rate | About 79% fixed; weighted average rate 4.88% on total debt | Documentary Fact | CP-1 debt register |
| Reported covenant leverage ratio | 3.69 against 5.00 maximum | Management Language (issuer-reported) | CP-1 liquidity and covenant table |
| Analyst gross and net leverage | 4.15x and 4.01x | Analyst Interpretation | CP-1 C7 |
| Analyst interest cover | 4.87x on cash interest; 4.84x on interest expense | Analyst Interpretation | CP-1 C8 |
| Fair value of debt instruments | USD 4,833.2 million against carrying value USD 5,172.9 million | Documentary Fact | CP-1 debt register |
### Latest quarter and after

Q3 2026 revenue was USD 1,107.3 million and operating income USD 252.9 million, including an USD 11.2 million divestiture gain; excluding that line operating income rose 6.6%. The revolver was reduced by USD 130.0 million in the quarter, the company repurchased 658,460 shares and paid a quarterly dividend of USD 0.36 per share. After quarter end it repurchased 232,968 shares for USD 18.2 million and lowered its 2026 earnings outlook on October 28, 2026 [CP-1 latest quarter; CP-1A timeline]. Nothing dated after October 29, 2026 is supplied.
## Calculations
Inputs are the upstream handoff figures cited. Results are rounded as shown.

- **C1, coverage of near-term maturities.** Liquidity USD 1,686.4 million (CP-1 C11) / current maturities USD 195.06 million (195,060 thousand) = 8.6x. Liquidity / the April 2027 and December 2027 notes, 136.924 + 550.000 = USD 686.924 million = 2.5x.

- **C2, notes at fair value.** Fair value of the six senior note series at September 30, 2026 (thousands): 138,043 + 544,087 + 731,062 + 767,049 + 725,776 + 770,896 = 3,676,913; face value 3,886,924 (CP-1 debt register); 3,676,913 / 3,886,924 = 94.6%. The fair values are Level 2 market-price estimates (Q3 10-Q page:19, page:20).

- **C3, leverage illustration (analyst definitions, not the covenant).** Carrying total debt 5,172,948 thousand / 5.00 = 1,034,590 thousand of EBITDA; against analyst LTM EBITDA of 1,246,945 thousand (CP-1 C1) this is a fall of 17.0%. The reported covenant ratio is on an unsupplied definition, so this is not covenant headroom.

- **C4, floating-rate sensitivity (inference).** Treating the term loan, revolver and headquarters facility as the floating-rate debt, 735,938 + 235,000 + 110,852 = 1,081,790 thousand (CP-1 C11); a 100 basis point rise adds 1,081,790 x 1% = 10,818 thousand, USD 10.8 million, on an annual basis, or 4.2% of LTM cash interest of USD 256.3 million (CP-1 C4). The 10-K shows a 10% proportional rise adding USD 5.9 million at December 31, 2025 (10-K page:66). The instruments' floating status is inferred, not listed in the sources.

- **C5, upstream figures reused.** Gross leverage 4.15x, net leverage 4.01x, cover 4.87x, operating cash flow less capex USD 681.4 million and 13.2% of debt, distributions and shortfalls, and mix and concentration percentages are taken from CP-1 (C7, C8, C3, C10) and CP-1A (C1 to C3) and are not recomputed.
## Gaps
| Gap | Why it matters | Severity | Action |

| Covenant ratio definition and credit agreement terms (payment restrictions, baskets, guarantors) not supplied; no EBITDA in any source | Headroom, legal capacity for distributions and ranking cannot be verified | High | Supply the credit agreement and covenant compliance definition |

| Indentures, security and guarantor detail for the senior notes not supplied | Ranking and structural position of USD 3,886.9 million of notes unassessed | High | Supply the indentures and guarantor schedule |
| Ratings and market prices other than fair values not supplied | No external credit opinion to compare against | Medium | Supply rating reports or keep Not supplied |
| Ownership percentages, board and related-party detail (proxy statement not supplied) | Governance and control rights cannot be assessed | Medium | Supply the 2026 proxy statement |
| Floating-rate and maturity-table conflicts | Interest sensitivity and the maturity ladder are on a stated basis only | Medium | Confirm in the filed HTML or with the issuer |
| Revenue and profit by state; customer and supplier concentration | Regional concentration risk unquantified | Medium | Request disclosure |
| Unclaimed property audits unquantified; part of cash encumbered | Contingent claim and liquidity are not fully measured | Medium | Carry as limits; request amounts |
| Events from October 30, 2026 to the cutoff | New financing or ratings could change the view | Medium | Supply later filings or confirm none |
## Next module

- CP-5: check every figure here against its upstream table; the key attributed items are the reported covenant ratio, the outlook change and the market share claim. Keep the estimated leverage labelled as an analyst estimate on the printed operating income and depreciation and amortization lines.
